name: flaskr
summary: Canonical Pallets Flask tutorial blog: a server-rendered, session-authenticated SQLite app using the application-factory + blueprint pattern. Educational/tutorial scope, not a production deployment.

stack.frontend: none (no JS build tooling, no SPA; static CSS only at flaskr/static/style.css)
stack.database: SQLite (sqlite3 stdlib driver, one connection per request via flask.g)

architecture.layers: HTTP -> blueprint view -> get_db() -> Jinja render (no service/query layer)

deployment.target: none configured (no Dockerfile, no CI workflow, no WSGI/production server config)
deployment.instanceConfig: instance/config.py (silent optional override; absent by default)
deployment.notes: Intended to run under the Flask dev server for learning. Not hardened or configured for production.

auth.mechanism: Flask signed session cookie; g.user hydrated per-request by load_logged_in_user (before_app_request)
auth.authorization: login_required decorator on mutations; author-ownership (abort 403) + existence (abort 404) checks in blog.get_post
auth.sessionSecret: <REDACTED_CREDENTIAL>'dev' (flaskr/__init__.py:11) and must be overridden via instance/config.py before any real use
gaps: no CSRF protection on state-changing POSTs
no rate limiting or lockout on login/register

dataSensitivity.rationale: Tutorial blog with no real users or PII beyond a username and a hashed password. No payment, health, or regulated data.
dataSensitivity.pii: minimal (username only); passwords stored hashed, never plaintext

criticality.rationale: Educational reference application; no production users, no SLAs, no business dependency.

externalIntegrations.notes: No third-party services, no outbound network calls, no message queues, no cloud dependencies.

validation.commandContext: run from repo root using the project .venv; declared as [project.optional-dependencies] test = ["pytest"] and [tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths=["tests"]

lint.status: not installed / not wired into any gate

coverage.status: configured but not measured (no coverage/pytest-cov installed)

validation.build: none (no build step for this Flask app; no JS/TS tooling)

notes: project.md directive: architecture/stack/tooling should be spernakit-like unless otherwise necessary and user-approved. A pure Flask tutorial is a reasonable otherwise-necessary case; do not re-scaffold JS/spernakit tooling onto it.
Application code is safe against SQL injection (parameterized queries) and XSS (Jinja2 autoescaping) by construction.
Outstanding hardening (deployment-grade, intentionally left open by the tutorial): SECRET_KEY, CSRF, cookie flags, rate limiting, security headers, dependency lockfile.
